input.jd:
We're Lumen Health, a 30-person company building scheduling software for outpatient clinics. We're hiring a full-stack engineer to join the team that owns the patient-facing booking flow.

Day to day you'll be shipping features in React and Node, working closely with our two designers, and talking to clinic staff about what's broken. We deploy several times a day and everyone touches production.

You'll need at least three years of professional experience with React and TypeScript, and you should be comfortable owning a feature end to end, from a rough Figma to a monitored deploy. We work in the open, so you'll need to be able to explain your decisions in writing to people who aren't engineers.

It would be great if you've worked in healthcare before, or with HIPAA-regulated data, but it isn't essential. Same for GraphQL — we use it, but you can learn it here.

We're remote across US time zones.

comfortable owning a feature end to end
explain your decisions in writing to people who aren't engineers

nice.text: worked in healthcare before, or with HIPAA-regulated data

input.jd:
Software Engineer — Pilot

Pilot is an AI assistant that runs inside your existing tools. You'll build the surfaces where users hand Pilot a task and watch it work.

Most of what you ship falls into three areas:

Agent UX — showing live progress, streaming partial results, letting users interrupt and approve steps.
Integrations — the connectors that let users plug Notion, Linear, GitHub, and Google Calendar into Pilot.
Channels — keeping the web app consistent with Pilot's presence in Slack and Microsoft Teams.

What's hard: the system is probabilistic. "Working on it" is a real UX problem.

What we're looking for
A track record of shipping real products. The ability to take a vague brief and turn it into something usable within a week. Experience with agent or LLM products is a plus.
